title: Flat locally quasi-finite scheme morphisms preserve coheight
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally quasi-finite (quasi-finite at every source point [pqf-def-quasifinite]). For any $z\in X$, the coheight of $f(z)$ equals the coheight of $z$. Coheight is the supremum of the lengths of strict chains of generalizations ending at the specified point, in the specialization order; for a scheme point it equals the Krull dimension of its stalk [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: This is the existing proved source-library declaration Scheme.Hom.coheight_apply_of_flat, read at lines 94–115. It is attached, not restated in Lean. A locally quasi-finite fibre has no distinct comparable points. Thus a specialization and its reverse between image points force equality upstairs, making f strictly monotone in the specialization order.

Flatness makes f generalizing: every strict generalization of f(z) lifts to a generalization of z. The lift is strict because its image is strict. The order-theoretic coheight equality theorem for a strictly monotone map with this lifting property gives the asserted equality. The source proof closes this argument without sorry. Empty sources have no point z; zero and infinite coheight are both covered by the order-theoretic statement.
